title: ML use case
description: One ML use case. File name: registry/ml_use_cases/<department>__<use_case_id>.yaml. The platform's Terraform reads it and creates the use case's identity and access (ml-project module).

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the file was written for. Only 1.x is supported.

use_case_id.description: Short name of the use case, e.g. tool-wear. The same name as the model, the repo (ml-<id>) and the OneLake folder.

department.description: Department that owns the use case. A file registry/ml_workspaces/<department>.yaml must exist.

display_name.description: Human-readable name, e.g. Tool wear prediction.

status.description: active: provisioned. retired: kept for the record; Terraform removes its identity and access.

owner.description: Model owner: a person or team, e.g. an email address or team name.

github_repo.description: The use case's repo, as org/repo. Only workflows from this repo can log in to Azure.

github_ids.description: Optional: numeric IDs of the repo owner and the repo, only when GitHub puts them in the OIDC subject (repo:org@<owner_id>/repo@<repo_id>). Find them with: gh api repos/<org>/<repo> --jq '.owner.id, .id'.

github_create_repo.description: true (default) = the platform creates the repo from the template. false = the repo already exists.

reviewer_github_ids.description: GitHub user IDs who approve model versions (the approval gate of deploy.yml). Find one with: gh api users/<login> --jq .id

risk_tier.description: Set at qualification (step 2): how strict the approval gate is.

gpu.description: true = the use case's own cluster has a GPU instead of CPU only. Needs GPU quota from Microsoft first.

reads.description: Tables the use case reads, as <domain>.<layer>.<table>. Read access is granted by the data owner.

predictions_table.description: Gold table the predictions are written to. Must start with ml_ (consumer table for ML).
